value.system_prompt: You output raw JSON only. No markdown fences, no prose.

parameters.content:
## The model does not score the lead

The model returns labels from a closed enum set and a quote for each one. This
node turns labels into points with fixed weights, so the same lead always gets
the same number and every point is traceable to a named component.

It also checks each quote against the text the model was given. A quote that is
not there is a fabrication: it costs 10 points and forces human review, rather
than quietly passing through as supporting evidence.

parameters.jsCode:
const raw = $input.first().json;
const r = (raw && raw.json) ? raw.json : raw;
const fx = $("Lead Fixture Loop").first().json;
const modifierNames = ((r.scoring || {}).modifiers || []).map(function (m) { return m.modifier; });
return [{ json: {
  case_id: fx.case_id,
  note: fx.note,
  expect_score: fx.expect_score,
  expect_tier: fx.expect_tier,
  expect_action: fx.expect_action,
  expect_outreach: fx.expect_outreach,
  expect_review: fx.expect_review,
  expect_modifier: fx.expect_modifier,
  expect_rubric: fx.expect_rubric,
  actual_score: r.score,
  actual_tier: r.tier,
  actual_action: r.recommended_action,
  actual_outreach: r.outreach_allowed,
  actual_review: r.requires_human_review,
  actual_rubric: (r.scoring || {}).rubric_version,
  rubric_source: (r.scoring || {}).rubric_source,
  rubric_error: (r.scoring || {}).rubric_error,
  tenant_id: r.tenant_id,
  trace_id: r.trace_id,
  modifiers: modifierNames,
  confidence: r.confidence,
  signals_source: (r.provenance || {}).signals_source,
  model_provider: (r.provenance || {}).model_provider,
  verified: (r.verification || {}).verified,
  unsupported_evidence: ((r.grounding || {}).unsupported_evidence || []).length,
  unreadable_signals: (r.scoring || {}).unreadable_signals || [],
  canonicalised: (r.scoring || {}).canonicalised || [],
  latency_ms: r.latency_ms
} }];

parameters.content:
## Rubric suite

Eight fixtures hand the rubric its signals directly, so each one asserts an exact
score rather than a range. Q04 is the interesting one: a CTO with an approved
budget and an immediate timeline still scores 15, because the use case is
outside the ICP and no amount of buying intent overrides that.

Q09 runs the real model end to end. Its score is not predictable, so it asserts
structure only: a score in range, a known tier, and a recorded provider.

description: Scores an inbound lead against a deterministic rubric. The model only returns labels from a closed enum set plus a verbatim quote per label; fixed weights turn labels into points, and every quote is checked against the source text before it can earn any.
